_doc: Pilot place prompts, v2 2026-11-25 (user: keep the top-down view but paint each place as its own picture at true, grand scale, not a miniature in a map tile; detail the prompt). where = the real geography, read from the record AND the map crop (in_<id>.png); imagined = the writer's picture of one moment (not sent); subject = the precise description that is sent, after the fixed place style block in paint_authored.py.

places.name: Băng Tâm Các
places.where: Region 7 (Ngọc Hồ Sơn), far north. On the map the place is a large island of black lava in a cold sea, about ten tiles (some 250 km) across, with smaller rocky islets off its eastern shore. Tundra, sea level at the coast. The volcano Chúc Long Sơn stands about 125 km away; it buried the old school Hồ Thiên Phái under lava in 425. Water 61 %, Ice 22. The great sect of Ice: about 150-200 cultivators and thousands of residents with servants, artisans, candidates and families; the Vessel Hall (the head's court), the Array Hall under it, the Plum Sword Hall, the Hall of Cold Law, the disciples' quarters; the Jade Vessel Array laid into the ice over the buried vent in 470.
places.imagined: A clear winter afternoon, low gold sun, seen from as high as a cloud. The island is enormous and runs off the edges of the picture, black lava frosted white, with fjords and ice cliffs along the near coast. Over the heart of the island the founder laid a sheet of blue glacier ice some ten kilometres across, as flat as a frozen lake, and on it stands a white city of ice: an outer town of hundreds of white houses, workshops and storehouses for the servants and artisans, laid out on straight frozen streets and canals; inside it a second wall; then terrace after terrace of halls rising up a black lava mountain the cultivators carved into steps, every terrace walled and gated, with long covered galleries and bridges of ice joining them. On the summit, the Vessel Hall, as big as an emperor's palace, and behind it a white pagoda thirty storeys high. Beneath the whole city, under the ice, a ring of jade-green light kilometres wide glows up through the ice, steam rising along it. At the foot of the mountain, the green-tiled roof of the old buried pagoda sticks out of a lava field the sect has kept bare as a memorial. Sledges and ice-elk trains on the frozen roads, and specks of people everywhere.
places.subject: The place: Băng Tâm Các, the great sect of Ice, a white city of halls built by cultivators on a vast black lava island in a cold northern sea. Setting: seen from very high above at a steep aerial angle; the island is enormous and runs off the edges of the frame, its black lava frosted white, with ice cliffs and fjords along the near coast and a dark sea scattered with drifting ice beyond; small rocky islets off the eastern shore; far away on the horizon a dark volcano sends up one thin thread of smoke. The ice: over the heart of the island lies a sheet of flat, glassy blue glacier ice about ten kilometres across. The sect, at true and grand scale, fills most of the frame: (1) an outer town on the ice of hundreds of white-walled houses, workshops, storehouses and stables with grey-blue tile roofs, laid out along straight frozen streets and canals, enclosed by a high white outer wall with great gate towers; (2) inside it a second, higher wall; (3) at the centre a black lava mountain carved by the cultivators into nine broad walled terraces, each terrace lined with large white halls, courtyards and plum gardens, joined by long covered galleries, stairways and arched bridges of clear ice; (4) on the summit the Vessel Hall, a white palace as large as an emperor's, on a white stone platform, and behind it a slender white pagoda some thirty storeys high, the tallest thing on the island. Signature elements: beneath the whole city, under the ice, a ring of glowing jade-green light kilometres wide shines up through the ice like a halo, with soft walls of steam rising along it; and at the foot of the mountain the green-tiled, curled roof-tip of an old pagoda sticks up out of a bare black lava field kept as a memorial, the only green in the white city. Life at scale: sledges and trains of pale ice-elk on the frozen roads, and thousands of tiny figures in white on the streets and terraces. Light: low golden winter sun from the upper left, long blue shadows to the lower right, a cold clear sky.

places.name: Hàn Giao Chử
places.where: Region 7, 5.7 tiles (about 140 km, some nine days' road) from the seat. On the map: a low islet of black rock in the open cold sea. A cold giao (flood-dragon) once coiled here, and its body is remembered in the great coiling ridge of pressure ice around the islet. Water 59 %, Ice 14. Băng Tâm Các's outer gate: the Beast Hall (ice beasts, the sect's mounts), the guest alchemist's hall outside the array, the stewards; the Frost Test is sat on the sea ice beside the islet until dawn.
places.imagined: Dawn after a Frost Test night. The sea around the black islet is frozen in a wide white skirt, and the old pressure ridge of ice coils three times around the islet like the body of a white serpent, its head-end lifted where it cracked last thaw. On the rock, inside a low white wall, the outer gate: long low stables for the ice beasts with steam coming from their doors, a few white halls, a courtyard where a white ice-elk is being led out. Outside the wall on a separate spur, the guest alchemist's squat stone hall with a tall chimney breathing white steam. On the sea ice beside the islet, a perfectly smooth round field of glassy blue ice where about thirty candidates sit in rows, white with frost, some slumped, while two stewards in white walk between them. Bones of old prey on the rocks.
places.subject: The place: Hàn Giao Chử, the outer gate and beast hall of Băng Tâm Các, on a low islet of black rock in a frozen northern sea. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at dawn, the islet in the centre of the frame and the sea ice around it. The sea is frozen in a wide white skirt around the islet, with open dark-blue water beyond its edge. Signature element: a huge ridge of pressure ice, white and blue, coils three times around the islet like the body of a giant serpent, thick as a city wall, cracked in places, one end rising like a lifted head. On the rock, inside a low white stone wall: four long low stables for ice beasts with white steam drifting from their doors; three white halls with grey-blue tile roofs; a stone courtyard where a pale ice-elk with crystal antlers is being led out by a tiny figure. Outside the wall, on a separate rocky spur, the guest alchemist's squat grey stone hall with a tall square chimney breathing white steam. On the sea ice beside the islet, a perfectly smooth, round field of glassy pale-blue ice, about two hundred paces across, where some thirty tiny candidates sit cross-legged in neat rows, white with frost, a few slumped; two small figures in white walk between the rows. Bleached bones of old prey lie on the black rocks of the shore. Light: the first pink-gold dawn light from the upper left, long cold blue shadows, breath and steam hanging in the still air.

places.name: Tuần Tùng Đường
places.where: Region 4, the temperate pine sea. On the map: rolling hills under dense dark pine forest, with grey rock outcrops breaking through the trees and a river winding at the south-east; the hall stands on a hill about 450 m high, off the road, 9 tiles above the market Tùng Hạ Thị. Wood 43 %. A young sect (founded 1191) of road wardens and wolf hunters, about 40 people: the wardens' hall, the stables, the shooting yard; the pines' riders of the Coiled Root Hall lodge here. They live on wolf pelts and the pines' bounty on wolf ears.
places.imagined: Late afternoon in early winter, the first snow on the hilltop. The hill is a bald round crown of rock and grass rising out of an endless sea of dark pines, with grey crags poking through the forest around it. On the crown, a palisade of tall sharpened pine trunks makes a rough oval. Inside: the long wardens' hall of dark timber with a steep shingle roof and smoke from two chimneys, a stable block with horses in a paddock, sheds, a smithy glowing, and the shooting yard with straw targets and a line of wardens shooting. Over the gate hangs a row of grey wolf pelts. A watch platform is built high into the one great pine that stands inside the wall. A cart track winds down through the trees toward the river and the road. A caravan of six wagons is coming up the track.
places.subject: The place: Tuần Tùng Đường, the hall of the pine wardens, a young sect of road guards and wolf hunters on a hilltop in a sea of pines. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a late afternoon in early winter. An endless sea of dark green pine forest rolls over low hills to the horizon, broken by grey rock crags poking through the trees; a river winds through the forest in the lower right corner, catching the light. In the centre, one round hill rises above the forest with a bare crown of grey rock and pale grass, dusted with the first snow. The sect: on the crown, a rough oval palisade of tall sharpened pine trunks, at true scale, with a heavy timber gate on the downhill side; over the gate hangs a long row of grey wolf pelts. Inside: one long wardens' hall of dark weathered timber on a stone footing, with a steep dark shingle roof and smoke rising from two chimneys; a stable block and a paddock with a dozen horses; several sheds and a small smithy with an orange glow at its door; and a bare trampled shooting yard with a row of straw targets, where a line of tiny wardens stand shooting bows. Signature element: inside the wall stands one huge old pine, far taller than the rest, with a wooden watch platform and ladder built high into its branches. A cart track winds down the hill through the pines toward the river, and a small caravan of six covered wagons is climbing it. No pagodas, no tiled roofs, nothing ornate: rough, strong, practical. Light: low golden sun from the upper left, long blue shadows across the snow and the trees.
